messages:
Maria Chen: FYI — staging showed a weird spike when the v2 header toggle was flipped for a subset of clients. Routing to v2 looks fine, but client libraries retried aggressively and our quota/p95 token cost jumped. Need a short plan.
Ryan Patel: ugh. seen that. do we know if it was retries or just v2 tokens are larger for those requests? :thinking:
Sophia Gomez: quick telemetry: so far looks like 60% retries, rest is slightly bigger payloads. retries came from clients getting 429s from an overloaded v2 pool, then doing backoff=0. Immediate mitigation: suppress automatic client-side aggressive retries OR make server respond with a graceful fallback instead of 429.
Oliver Wu: prefer graceful fallback (route to v1) when we detect client is non-sensitive (non-enterprise tier). But that has semantics differences. Some customers depend on v2 behavior.
Kevin Brown: agree. also we should add a server-side "soft-backoff" header to communicate: `X-Redwood-Route-Action: fallback=v1; retry-after=10s` so clients can behave.
Maria Chen: proposal: introduce a fallback policy for the next 48h that does per-account decision based on `account.experimental_v2` flag and `quota_headroom`. If headroom < threshold -> route to v1 and emit metric `routing.v2.fallback_count`.
Ryan Patel: :+1: but need to be careful with console UX. We should show on the Model Route page a small banner: "Traffic shifted to v1 due to capacity/backoff" with link to rollback.
Sophia Gomez: telemetry additions we need now: `api.v2.429_rate`, `api.v2.retry_rate`, `routing.v2.fallback_count`, `client.retry_backoff_distribution`. Also create an alert: >2% sustained retry_rate spike for >5m.
infra-bot: INCIDENT-TRACKER: created incident 2026-03-18-17. ticket=INC-4873
Oliver Wu: on the fallback method itself — two choices: (A) immediate transparent reroute to compatible v1 model, preserving request, or (B) return a 429 with `X-Redwood-Route-Suggestion: v1` so client can choose. (A) is easiest for customers but hides regressions and could mask real v2 issues.
Sophia Gomez: we should do (A) for canary/ramping only. Add sampling for debug logs 0.5% of rerouted requests to keep us honest.
Kevin Brown: and we need to version-negotiation header for the wire: `X-Redwood-API-Version: v2` is already used. Add `X-Redwood-API-Route: prefer=v2; fallback=v1` for clients wanting priority. Server side should honor but not blindly fail.
Ryan Patel: UX for rollouts: new console toggle won't be a blunt switch. Suggest three modes: Off / Canary / Enforced. Canary uses percentage and per-account allowlist. Exposed in Console: Route -> Versions -> toggle with tooltip.
Maria Chen: rollout plan suggestion:
- Step 0: Patch server to emit `X-Redwood-Route-Action` and metric `routing.v2.fallback_count` (PR #4523)
- Step 1: Enable fallback behavior for 1% of traffic for 2h (canary) and 0.5% sampled debug logs
- Step 2: If stable, ramp to 10% over 24h, monitor retry_rate and latency
- Step 3: If stable at 10% for 24h, expand to 50% with enterprise opt-outs
- Step 4: Roll to 100% only after no regressions for 72h
Sophia Gomez: add console telemetry widget: small chart showing `v2 success rate`, `v2 429s`, `fallback rate` with a green/yellow/red state based on thresholds.
Ryan Patel: what's the short-term mitigation we can flip right now? Can we throttle retries server-side by returning `Retry-After` and `X-Redwood-Route-Action: hold` ?
Oliver Wu: yes. I'll push a lightweight change that returns `Retry-After: 10` and `X-Redwood-Route-Action: hold` when queue depth > 80% of v2 pool. That avoids immediate reroutes but buys time.
Kevin Brown: make sure that middleware sets `Cache-Control: private, max-age=0` for that response so proxies don't cache the hold.
Maria Chen: testing snippet for QA (use this to reproduce on staging):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer TEST" \
  -H "X-Redwood-API-Version: v2" \
  -d '{"inputs":"hello"}' \
  https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Look at response headers for `X-Redwood-Route-Action` / `Retry-After` and confirm fallback count increments in metrics.
Sophia Gomez: also add a quick sampling rule in observability to capture request/response diffs for rerouted requests: label `routing.debug_reroute`.
infra-bot: DEPLOYMENT: rollback-bot scheduled patch v2-backoff-guard -> deploy window 2026-03-18 19:00 UTC
Ryan Patel: question: should we treat enterprise customers differently? Some require strict v2. Proposal: honor `account.force_v2=true` and instead provide capacity isolation (move to dedicated pool) rather than reroute.
Maria Chen: yep. enterprise flag bypasses fallback. we must log `routing.v2.enterprised_bypass` and surface in console.
Oliver Wu: created PR #4523 with server header changes and PR #4525 for metrics. Will link.
Kevin Brown: quick ops checklist for deployment: add alert, update console banner copy, ensure KMS logs preserved if debug sampling enabled.
rollout-bot: ROLLOUT: scheduled canary at 2026-03-18T20:00:00Z -> 1% traffic for 2h. Monitoring channels: #eng-platform, #infra-alerts
Maria Chen: sounds good. assign owners: Oliver -> server change PRs, Sophia -> telemetry/dashboards, Ryan -> console UX and banner, Kevin -> ops checklist and alerts. I'll own rollout coordination.
Sophia Gomez: small UX copy suggestion for console banner: "Traffic shifted automatically to v1 to protect latency & quota. Click for details or to opt your account out." keeps it human.
Ryan Patel: any objections to enabling `soft-backoff` header behavior for next 48h? need quick thumbs.
Kevin Brown: :thumbsup:
Oliver Wu: :+1:
Sophia Gomez: fine by me
Maria Chen: OK. I'll merge PRs after a quick review and enable the canary. Will post updates in this thread. :eyes:
Maria Chen: (later) PRs merged, canary live. monitoring dashboard pinned in #eng-platform. If you see anomalies ping me.
